The 'prototype testing / design reviews / security automation' breadth traces to a single weak source (adam.holter.com). cross_company_notes: TIER DISTRIBUTION across all 36 company-tool pairings: T1 = 11, T2 = 9, T3 = 5, T4 = 11. STRONGEST CONFIRMED ADOPTION: NVIDIA (Cursor + Codex both T1 via official vendor case studies naming NVIDIA at huge scale), Microsoft (GitHub Copilot T1 with hard published dotnet/runtime + github.com dogfooding numbers and a Nadella quote), Google (Pichai earnings stat + AlphaEvolve, both T1, plus a deep internal Gemini stack), AMD (Claude Code T1 from a named director's quantified public GitHub issue), Cisco (Copilot T1 triangulated by GitHub + arXiv + Cisco IT), and MediaTek (two T1 home-built signals via Microsoft and NVIDIA case studies). SPARSEST: Marvell (one T1 but it is EDA-only formal verification, with NO general agentic coding agent and otherwise only thought-leadership), Broadcom (real internal adoption but the tool is NEVER NAMED, capped at T2), and Qualcomm (strongest signal is its OWN in-house tool at T2 with no third-party agentic agents). RECURRING TOOLS: Claude Code appears at almost every company (T1 AMD; T2 internal/T1-product Apple; T3 NVIDIA; T3 Cisco; T2-being-phased-out Microsoft; plausible-but-unconfirmed Broadcom backend) - the single most pervasive thread. OpenAI Codex recurs (T1 NVIDIA, T2 AMD, product-only Apple). Cursor recurs strongly only at NVIDIA (T1); elsewhere weak/external. GitHub Copilot is concentrated at Microsoft (vendor+dogfood) and Cisco (T1), and is notably RESTRICTED/banned at Apple and absent as internal use at the chip firms. VENDOR_MAKER vs DOGFOODING: Google and Microsoft both make AND use tools - the discipline here is to keep vendor_maker (Gemini CLI/Antigravity/Jules/Code Assist; GitHub Copilot product) separate from internal dogfooding (Cider/Goose/AlphaEvolve; dotnet/runtime). Apple, NVIDIA, Qualcomm and Broadcom all show the product-integration-vs-internal-use trap (Xcode SDK, NIM, CodeMate, Tanzu) which I scored separately. CONSISTENCY CONCERNS / RED FLAGS: (1) WebFetch HTTP 403 affected nearly every company - most quotes are search-snippet/headline paraphrases, not full-page reads; well-corroborated claims were not auto-downgraded but precise wording/numbers carry mild uncertainty. (2) Self-reported / vendor-reported scale figures recur everywhere (NVIDIA 30k/40k & 3x, Qualcomm 1,500+, Microsoft 67.9%, Cisco 3x, MediaTek 97%/88%, AMD's logs) - all directional, not independently audited. (3) Mis-attribution risks the source agents correctly flagged: Apple's '70-90%'/'Stripe 1,370' numbers belong to Anthropic/Stripe NOT Apple; Marvell's 35% figure was tied to an unnamed provider not verbatim Marvell; the Google/Block 'Goose' name collision; MediaTek's platform-wide 97%/88% being applied loosely to coding. (4) The 'ciscoittech' GitHub org's Cisco affiliation is unverified (kept at T3). (5) Broadcom's named '5x productivity' figure pertains to Tanzu PaaS generally, not the coding agents. (6) Several headline 'X% of code is AI-written' stats (Google 75%, follow-on figures) are secondary/social and should not be treated as confirmed exec quotes. Overall the dataset is internally consistent and the Phase-A/B agents were appropriately skeptical; the main systemic limitation is reliance on search snippets due to 403 fetch blocks plus uniformly self-reported scale numbers.
